## In plain English

Master CI fails verify:pack-drift because the pin-compiled pack-render resolves REPO_ROOT from import.meta.url inside @deftai/directive-runtime. That makes both pack sources and projection targets live inside the installed package, where deposit-link-rewrite has already rewritten relative links. The gate never looks at the checkout content/. Fix: on a framework source checkout, pack-render --check must use the project root (cwd / --project-root), so it compares repo projections to repo pack sources.

## Approaches

### Approach A (Prefer-A lean)
Make pack-render resolve REPO_ROOT/CONTENT_ROOT from an explicit project root (cwd default, optional --project-root) when that root is a framework source checkout (content/packs present). Module-location remains the fallback for consumer/OVPR layouts where the package IS the content root. Engine invoke / verify:pack-drift then checks tip content/ without waiting on a runtime release. Keep #5802 contentRoot precedence as a secondary guard once frameworkRoot is correct.

### Approach B
Bypass pin for verify:pack-drift only: Taskfile/engine tip-source tsx of packages/core/src/packs/pack-render.ts on framework check. Leaves the compiled pin broken for the same verb everywhere else.

### Approach C
Strip deposit-link-rewrite markers / rewrite deltas before compare, or special-case package-internal paths as non-drift. Treats the symptom; still never audits tip content/.

## Reject candidates (pre-panel)
- Softening verify:pack-drift to warn-only on master
- Shipping a runtime release solely so pin copies match tip (does not fix module-location root)
- Teaching contentRoot alone to fix this when frameworkRoot is already the package (#5802 already landed and still fails)

## Draft file_scope lean
- packages/core/src/packs/pack-render.ts (and shared root helper if packs-slice shares the same hole)
- packages/core/src/packs/pack-render.test.ts (+ adjacent packs-slice tests if shared)
- CHANGELOG.md
- tasks/packs.yml or engine invoke docs only as footnote if argv/--project-root needs a one-line discoverability note

Prefer A's root correction, but it cannot bind with its current no-release delivery claim.

### F1 — The changed renderer must reach the invoked pin
blocks-the-design

Evidence: pin-read at f0b2a3623a6be6ab2952bcafca0c8114b2b058cf confirms `tasks/packs.yml` dispatches through `:engine:invoke`; `tasks/engine.yml` explicitly selects the installed checkout pin under #5805, forbids tip-dist fallback, and names `task materialize:runtime` as tip dogfood without publish. Editing `packages/core/src/packs/pack-render.ts` alone leaves that invoked binary unchanged. Its existing parser also does not recognize `--project-root`.

Failure: A can fix the source implementation while the actual gate remains red, leaving P4 unmet. Task/engine delivery is a mechanism concern, not a documentation footnote.

Remedy: retain pin-exclusive dispatch and make the corrected runtime available through the existing materialization path before the gate, with a clean-checkout integration check of the actual task. If that path cannot serve CI, explicitly choose a corrected published pin or seek an authorized dispatch-contract change; do not claim source-only edits remove the release dependency.

### F2 — Correct frameworkRoot still does not guarantee checkout content
blocks-the-design

Evidence: `packages/core/src/content-root.ts` at the dispatch SHA deliberately lets a staged `@deftai/directive-content` package win over in-repo `content/`; #5802 changes precedence only for hoisted `directive-runtime`. A retains this helper as its secondary guard.

Failure: a source checkout with a staged content package still audits package sources/projections despite selecting the right project root. For lessons, the renderer can even pair package pack input with checkout `meta/lessons.md`. P1/P3 are not fully relieved by correcting REPO_ROOT alone.

Remedy: after positively identifying framework-source mode, bind pack inputs and document outputs directly to that checkout's `content/`, and lessons output to its `meta/lessons.md`. Preserve the existing content resolver for consumer mode. Verify with competing staged package content and a deliberately stale checkout projection; the latter must fail.

### F3 — Invocation cwd is not the framework checkout identity
sharpens-framing

Evidence: `tasks/packs.yml` preserves `USER_WORKING_DIR`; `tasks/engine.yml` separately resolves the source pin from `DEFT_ROOT` specifically to support subdirectory invocation. The draft identifies source mode by `content/packs` under cwd and otherwise falls back to module location.

Failure: invoking from a checkout subdirectory can select the package again. Conversely, an unrelated consumer's `content/packs` directory can be mistaken for framework source. Existing deposit-marker/source-buildability discrimination in `tasks/engine-invoke.cjs` is relevant prior art.

Remedy: pass the known framework root explicitly from the task, distinguish source from deposit using existing identity rules, and refuse an invalid explicit root rather than silently falling back. Resolve registry/default/containment paths from the same per-invocation root; import-time globals must not retain another worktree's root. Test subdirectory invocation and two successive explicit roots, while preserving traversal/symlink containment checks. This sharpens A's root contract without requiring a new general resolver framework.

### F4 — Panel metadata repair
footnote

The ceiling deposit 6357326269 names seat families and N≥3 but lacks operative `round:` and `siblings:` fields required by Envelope and ceiling. Parent should repair the protocol record without changing this round's input ceiling. This does not change the product remedy.

Road not taken: B is attractive because tip-source execution immediately exercises the fix, but it conflicts with the explicit #5805 pin-exclusive dispatch contract. An authorized exception would change that assessment. C cannot prove checkout projection freshness and should remain rejected.

Verification scope: HEAD equals the dispatch SHA; source and dispatch anchors were checked with `git show` and local searches. ## Verdict

Approach A is the right axis and the reject list is sound. But as drafted it is **under-limbed in two places and over-claims in one**. C1 makes the drafted flag inert; C3 shows the pain bind P1–P4 is scoped to the read path while the write path is the worse hazard; C7 shows A alone cannot deliver the issue's stated Expected. All three are mechanism-shaped, not wording.

## Findings

**C1 — load-bearing. The drafted flag cannot reach the roots it names.**
`REPO_ROOT`/`CONTENT_ROOT` are import-time module consts (`pack-render.ts:26-27`) and are already baked into `DEFAULT_SOURCE`/`DEFAULT_OUTPUT` (`:29-30`), every `RENDER_REGISTRY` entry (`:282-335`), and the containment realpath anchor (`:238`). An argv `--project-root` parsed in `parseArgs` (`:584`) reaches none of them. "Resolve REPO_ROOT/CONTENT_ROOT from an explicit project root" is one sentence hiding a de-constification limb. Without it A lands as a no-op flag that still reads the package.
Limb: `buildRenderRegistry(root)` as a function of the resolved root; thread the root into the containment resolver; `resolveRepoRoot()` survives only as the fallback branch.

**C2 — fail-closed association. Containment anchor becomes caller-controlled.**
Today the #2914 escape check anchors to a module-derived root no caller can move. A project-root input makes that anchor caller-supplied — this is the one place the Bound must speak rather than footnote. Keep the shape fail-closed: take the source-checkout branch only on a positive probe (`<root>/content/packs/` present), never on a bare `content/` directory a consumer project may legitimately own; containment re-anchors to the *resolved* root; unprobeable root falls back to module-location rather than widening the write surface.

**C3 — the pain bind is scoped to `--check`; the write path is worse.**
`packs:render` routes through the same pinned binary with no `--check` (`tasks/packs.yml:39-44`), and registry `output` is `join(REPO_ROOT, "meta/lessons.md")`. On a source checkout the pin therefore **writes projections into `node_modules/.../@deftai/directive-runtime/`** and leaves tip `content/` untouched. The gate's own failure text says "Run task packs:render to regenerate" — i.e. the prescribed remedy is a silent mutation of the installed package. P1–P4 read as "false red"; this is "prescribed wrong write." Widen P1 or add P5; the remedy must cover render, not only check.

**C4 — scope: `packs-slice` is the same hole, already seamed.**
`packs-slice.ts:9-18` duplicates `resolveRepoRoot` verbatim and derives its own `CONTENT_ROOT`; `effectiveRepoRoot(repoRoot?)` (`:20-22`) is an existing override seam. From the pin, `task packs:slice` serves agents pack content out of the installed package, not tip. Promote the draft's conditional footnote ("if packs-slice shares the same hole") to a named limb on one shared helper — do not land a third copy of the resolver.

**C5 — prior art; A needs no new surface.**
The repo already has this convention: `--project-root` flag (`architecture/sor-preflight.ts:1290-1294`, `cache/main.ts:50-57`) plus `DEFT_PROJECT_ROOT` env (`capacity/backfill.ts:467`), and `dir: '{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}'` already sets per-invocation cwd (`tasks/packs.yml:41`). Reuse flag → env → cwd precedence as-is. This also deletes the draft's Taskfile/engine-docs footnote from file_scope — nothing new to make discoverable.

**C6 — the hole is currently untestable, which is why #5802 repeated.**
`pack-render.test.ts:27` recomputes `contentRoot(REPO_ROOT)` from the same module location, so every existing test runs in the single layout where the defect cannot appear. That is the structural reason a landed precedence fix still failed. Regression limb: one test driving `main` against a tmp fixture root that is **not** an ancestor of the module, asserting sources and outputs resolve under the fixture.

**C7 — A over-claims release-independence.**
`engine:invoke` is pin-exclusive on framework source by #5805 Prefer-A Bound — "no packages/runtime/dist fallthrough; missing pin fails closed" (`tasks/engine.yml:76-85`). So `verify:pack-drift` runs the pin's compiled `pack-render` regardless. A's "checks tip content/ without waiting on a runtime release," and the issue's "Master CI goes green without depending on a runtime release," are both unmet: A greens master only once a runtime release carrying A is pinned. State the sequencing in the Bound instead of inheriting the claim.

Corollary on Approach B: the draft's objection ("leaves the compiled pin broken") understates it. A tip-source `tsx` escape hatch for this verb reopens a Bound #5805 deliberately closed — that is a mechanism/fail-closed association change requiring a remint of #5805, not a Taskfile footnote. Reject B on that ground, which is stronger and cheaper than the draft's.

Approach C reject stands and can be sharpened: stripping deposit-rewrite deltas before compare makes the gate blind to genuine link-shape drift, trading a false red for a false green.

## Proposed Bound shape (short mechanism limbs)

1. Resolve the render root once per invocation — flag → `DEFT_PROJECT_ROOT` → cwd — taking the source-checkout branch only on a positive `content/packs/` probe; module-location is the fallback.
2. Make the render registry and containment anchor functions of that resolved root (removes the import-time consts).
3. Apply to render and check alike — the write path is in scope.
4. Share one root helper with `packs-slice`; no third copy.
5. One regression test exercising a root outside the module's ancestry.
6. Bound records that greening master requires a runtime release carrying this; no pin-exclusivity exception.

Footnotes only: CHANGELOG wording, `--project-root` help text. No Taskfile surface change needed (C5).

## file_scope delta vs draft

- add: `packages/core/src/packs/packs-slice.ts` (+ its test) — promoted from conditional
- add: shared root helper location (C4)
- drop: `tasks/packs.yml` / engine invoke docs (C5)
- keep: `pack-render.ts`, `pack-render.test.ts`, `CHANGELOG.md`

## Summary

`task verify:pack-drift` (`packs:verify-drift` → `engine:invoke` → `pack-render --check`) runs the **pinned runtime's** compiled `pack-render`. It never checks the repo's own `content/` projections. Instead it compares a fresh render against the copies shipped inside the installed `@deftai/directive-runtime` package, and those copies are deposit-link-rewritten, so the gate is always red on a source checkout. The problem is still present with the 0.128.0 pin.

## Evidence

The gate fails identically on master at `f0b2a3623` (pin 0.127.0) and on the same commit bumped to the 0.128.0 pin:

```
pack-drift: 7 projection(s) out of sync:
  node_modules/.pnpm/@deftai+directive-runtime@<pin>/node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime/meta/lessons.md
  .../skills/deft-directive-setup/SKILL.md
  .../coding/build-output.md
  .../coding/coding.md
  .../coding/testing.md
  .../strategies/README.md
  .../swarm/swarm.md
Run `task packs:render` to regenerate.
```

All 7 paths are inside the installed runtime package, not the repo tree.

Example of why the package copy can never match a fresh render (`content/coding/testing.md` vs the package's `coding/testing.md`):

```diff
 <!-- AUTO-GENERATED by task packs:render -- DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY -->
+<!-- deft:deposit-link-rewrite v=1 source="content/coding/testing.md" -->
 ...
-**See also**: [main.md](../../main.md) | ...
+**See also**: [main.md](../main.md) | ...
```

Master CI run [39891549225](https://github.com/deftai/directive/actions/runs/39891549225) at `f0b2a3623` failed **only** on this gate. Its vitest run was fully green (1478 files / 22833 tests passed), and both merge-gate jobs ended with `Failed to run task "verify:pack-drift"`, listing the same 7 paths under `@deftai+directive-runtime@0.127.0`.

Running the repo-source renderer against the same tree is clean:

```
tsx -e "import { main } from './packages/core/src/packs/pack-render.ts'; process.exit(main(['--check']))"
pack-drift: all 55 projection(s) in sync.
```

## Likely cause (read-only analysis)

`packages/core/src/packs/pack-render.ts`:

```ts
export function resolveRepoRoot(): string {
  return resolve(dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "..", "..", "..", "..");
}
const REPO_ROOT = resolveRepoRoot();
const CONTENT_ROOT = contentRoot(REPO_ROOT);
```

`REPO_ROOT` comes from the module's own location. When the module runs from the installed runtime (`vendor/directive-core/dist/packs/pack-render.js`), that location is the package root, not the project being checked. `contentRoot()` then returns the flattened package, so both the pack sources and the projection targets resolve inside the package. The #5802 `contentRoot` precedence fix doesn't help, because the framework root passed in is already the package.

## Expected

On a framework source checkout, `verify:pack-drift` checks the repo's own projections (`meta/lessons.md`, `content/**`) against the repo's pack sources, using the project root (cwd / `--project-root`) rather than the module location. Master CI goes green without depending on a runtime release.

Part of the pin/master skew tracked in #5848.
